title: Compatible isomorphisms of adic quotients induce an isomorphism of completions
statement: Let $(A,I)$ and $(B,J)$ be commutative rings with ideals, and let $e_n:A/I^n\xrightarrow{\sim}B/J^n$ be ring isomorphisms for $n\geq1$ that commute with all quotient transition maps. Then the induced map $E:\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/I^n\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1}B/J^n$ is a ring isomorphism. Writing $p_n^A$ and $p_n^B$ for the quotient projections from the respective inverse limits, it is the unique map satisfying $p_n^B\circ E=e_n\circ p_n^A$ for every $n\geq1$. Completion means the adic completion of [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion].

source.place: Tag 00MA(3), inverse-limit description of completion and the compatible finite-level maps

proof.text: Use [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] to write the two limits as compatible tuples with componentwise ring operations. For $1\leq m\leq n$ denote the quotient transitions by $a_{nm}:A/I^n\to A/I^m$ and $b_{nm}:B/J^n\to B/J^m$; the hypothesis is $b_{nm}e_n=e_ma_{nm}$. Define $E((x_n)_n)=(e_n(x_n))_n$. This tuple is compatible because $b_{nm}(e_n(x_n))=e_m(a_{nm}(x_n))=e_m(x_m)$. Since each $e_n$ preserves $0,1,+,\cdot$, the componentwise operations show that $E$ is a ring homomorphism and $p_n^B E=e_n p_n^A$.

source.place: Tag 00M9 (section-completion), definition of completion as compatible sequences; coordinatewise inverse-limit argument

proof.text: The inverse ring isomorphisms satisfy $a_{nm}e_n^{-1}=e_m^{-1}b_{nm}$: compose $b_{nm}e_n=e_ma_{nm}$ on the left with $e_m^{-1}$ and on the right with $e_n^{-1}$. Hence $H((y_n)_n)=(e_n^{-1}(y_n))_n$ is a compatible tuple whenever $(y_n)_n$ is, and defines a ring homomorphism in the reverse direction by the same componentwise operation identities. At coordinate $n$, $HE(x)$ equals $e_n^{-1}e_n(x_n)=x_n$, and $EH(y)$ equals $e_ne_n^{-1}(y_n)=y_n$. Equality of tuples gives $HE=1$ and $EH=1$, so $E$ is a ring isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00M9 (section-completion), definition of completion as compatible sequences; coordinatewise inverse-limit argument

proof.text: If $F:\varprojlim A/I^n\to\varprojlim B/J^n$ is any map with $p_n^BF=e_np_n^A$ for every $n\geq1$, then for each tuple $x$ its $n$th output coordinate is $p_n^B(F(x))=e_n(x_n)=p_n^B(E(x))$. Thus $F(x)=E(x)$ as tuples for every $x$, and $F=E$. This proves the stated uniqueness, even among maps of sets.
